targetTest: SwapNoticeBanner renders the current swap as a polite three-row status
expected: A populated Opus→Sonnet SwapNotice (model sonnet-live, provider OpenRouter, token label cred:sonnet, reason no live Opus triple, safeguardsApplies false) renders a polite banner: role=status, aria-live=polite, the network-body-warning amber surface, the lucide ArrowDown icon, three content rows (Opus is replaced by Sonnet since HH:mm / Serving sonnet-live on OpenRouter · token cred:sonnet · no live Opus triple / the safeguards sentence), mono model and credential values with title tooltips, break-words wrapping, no button, no destructive or Badge-warning styling, and no raw secret or message marker. A null notice renders an empty string.
actual: The RED SwapNoticeBanner stub renders empty markup: the first assertion fails at /role="status"/ with actual "" (the empty banner mismatch). The three sibling populated-banner assertions fail identically on the empty string (long-value, zh copy, safeguards-hidden), while the null-notice case passes because the stub already returns null for a missing notice.
semanticAssessment: The failure is the deliberate RED-only stub behavior reached through the real compiled component test: esbuild compiled packages/ui/src/pages/home/components/layout.tsx with the new SwapNoticeBanner export (returning null) plus the extended layout.test.tsx and observability.test.tsx, and renderToStaticMarkup produced an empty string for the populated notice — exactly the banner the GREEN task implements. Not a fixture/load failure: all 11 pre-existing tests in the file pass in the same process (valid TAP plan 1..15, exit 1). The observability file independently fails its 4 new SD-pill/expanded-detail assertions (SD pill count 0 !== 2, no network-body-warning block) using only existing RequestLogEntry fields, and its pre-existing response-header contract case passes unchanged (headers already flow through networkHeaderRows/LogJsonPanel with no UI code change). GREEN adds the banner implementation, i18n copy, App polling, MainLayout mount, and the network-logs SD pill/detail renderers.
